take_homes: You can't hand someone an agent. What carries over is context, a skill, an output or an interface, and someone still has to answer for it. That someone is probably me.
Ask what the teammate would have to drop to use mine, and talk to them before I build anything bigger.
Rolling out access and people actually using it are two different numbers. I've been counting the first.

monday.move: Before building the sales setup, sit down with one person from sales ops and ask how they do that job today. I'll write one assumption and one test in monday.md.
monday.who: The head of sales ops. I still need to check she's the right person, and I haven't named who maintains the setup.
monday.when: Tuesday, 20 minutes. Monday is sprint planning.
monday.stop_condition: If she already has something that works, or says she doesn't want it, I stop building the sales setup.
monday.blocker: Nobody outside engineering has asked for it, and I haven't named who would maintain it. I'll probably want to start building before I've talked to her.

misconception.why: The module never says directly that checking is for beginners. But 'checks' and 'accountability' are named as the parts that don't copy, and 'right the first time they try it' means skipping review costs me the non-engineers. I still think I can skip it on my own stuff.

one_line: Less about agents than I expected, more about why my rollouts stall. The accountability bit and the leadership story landed. Some of the exercise flow felt like ceremony.
